contents.name: §9.2 exact and backtracking line-search definitions, finite small-step argument, and geometric accepted-step bound
contents.reason: Supplies the canonical ray-minimization and Armijo interfaces. The local theorem separately proves exact-ray attainment on the compact open-domain sublevel required here.

contents.name: §9.3.1 strong-convexity gradient-gap inequality and exact-search contraction proof
contents.reason: The source proves the factor 1-m/M from the Hessian upper model and gradient-gap inequality. The local proof verifies the open-domain compact-ray selector and its hypotheses.

contents.name: §9.3.1 Armijo backtracking accepted-step and global gap-rate proof
contents.reason: The source establishes an accepted-step lower bound and linear gap decrease. The local proof derives the sharper contract constant min{1, 2b(1-a)/M} under the same curvature bound.

contents.name: §9.5.1–9.5.3 Newton direction, decrement, damped-phase decrease, finite phase, full-step acceptance, and quadratic estimate
contents.reason: Complete proof read. Its finite damped phase and local unit-step reasoning support the route; the local theorem preserves the canonical algorithm's positive decrement stopping boundary and proves the stated constants independently.

contents.name: §9.2–9.3.1 gradient-gap bound used as an intermediate in the residual estimate
contents.reason: The source gives the gradient-norm/objective-gap inequality; the local lemma supplies the complete open-convex-domain Hessian proof and also proves strong monotonicity.

contents.name: §9.2 conceptual gradient stopping discussion and §9.5.1 Newton decrement interpretation
contents.reason: These passages distinguish stopping quantities from objective error but do not certify a computed gradient with discrepancy delta. The true/computed-gradient distance bound is proved locally.

sources.title: Philip E. Gill and Margaret H. Wright, Math 171B Numerical Optimization Class Notes, September 1998
sources.locator: Complete 174-page notes fetched and inspected. Chapter 3 §§3.4.3–3.4.5, printed pp. 87–90 / physical PDF pp. 87–90; §3.5.1, printed pp. 90–93 / physical PDF pp. 90–93; §3.5.3–3.5.4, printed pp. 94–105 / physical PDF pp. 97–105. Exact line search, backtracking termination, modified-Newton global convergence, and eventual unit-step arguments were read in full.

contents.name: §3.5.1 exact line search definition, directional orthogonality, quadratic formula, and exact-search limitations
contents.reason: Independent textbook treatment of the ideal ray selector and its interior first-order condition. The local proof handles compact sublevel existence on an open domain.

contents.name: §3.4.3 steepest-descent direction and conditioning example on a positive-definite quadratic
contents.reason: Supports the chosen anisotropic quadratic witness and the distinction between objective-gap and iterate-error rates; all displayed arithmetic is verified locally.

contents.name: §3.5.1 backtracking definition, sufficient-decrease test, and finite termination argument
contents.reason: Independent full lecture-note derivation of Armijo backtracking and termination; the local proof establishes the stronger explicit accepted-step bound requested by the contract.

contents.name: §3.4.4–3.4.5 Newton direction and local pure-Newton quadratic statement
contents.reason: The notes state the classical local theorem under C3 regularity and a positive-definite critical Hessian. The library's canonical local supplier has the exact Lipschitz-Hessian and stopping hypotheses used here.

contents.name: Theorems 3.5.3–3.5.4: modified-Newton convergence to stationary points and eventual unit-step acceptance when the line-search parameter is below one half
contents.reason: Independent treatment of globalization and eventual full steps; its global theorem uses Hessian modification and stationarity rather than the stronger strongly-convex minimum claim proved locally.

contents.name: §3.5.1 and §3.4.5 exact-versus-local convergence discussion
contents.reason: Provides independent convexity and gradient-method context; the domain-local strong-convexity and strong-monotonicity implications are proved in the local lemma.

contents.name: Stopping and decrement distinctions in §§3.4–3.5
contents.reason: The notes distinguish residual/stopping quantities from convergence guarantees but do not cover a separate computed-gradient discrepancy; that certificate is proved locally.
